Everyone Grows
Empower
At Ardleigh Green Infant School we value every individual and the contribution they have to make to our school community. Our aim is for staff and children to reach their full potential within a caring, supportive and stimulating environment, characterised by excellence, enjoyment and high quality teaching and learning. pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome – Ardleigh Green Infant School
pageCache.text:
On behalf of the staff, children and governors, I would like to welcome you to Ardleigh Green Infant School.
As a school community we are very excited as we commence the next chapter in the life of Ardleigh Green Schools as we celebrate the past, embrace the present and look to the future with confidence, ensuring that our schools continue to be an exciting place to learn.
Our school has enthusiastic, talented and hardworking children, who are supported in their learning by an outstanding staff team, dedicated governors and very supportive parents. Our values of excellence, enjoyment, respect and equality, permeate the life of our school, with staff, pupils, governors and parents working and learning together, sharing a common aim for all our children to be the best that they can be.
We never underestimate the important role we play in your child’s life and therefore strive to make each day the best it can possibly be. We hope you enjoy many happy years with us and make lasting memories at Ardleigh Green.
If you wish to be kept up to date with events as they happen, please visit our news page or follow us on Twitter and Facebook.
With best wishes from everyone at Ardleigh Green Infant School
Mrs Verity HoffmanHeadteacher, Ardleigh Green Infant School

pageCache.pageTitle: About Us – Ardleigh Green Infant School
pageCache.text:
Ethos
The original school motto, “Strive to Succeed,” lives on and is achieved today through our staff children, parents and governors “Working Together, Learning Together and Growing Together.” We consider ourselves to be a forward thinking school, committed to meeting the academic, physical and emotional needs of every child. The school is well equipped to meet the technological demands of life in the 21st Century and our creative curriculum, with a focus on developing resourceful, resilient, reflective and responsible learners, ensures that all children leave our school well equipped to commence their junior school education.
A Strong Foundation
We are delighted that many of our children continue to go on to university after their secondary school education and are equally thrilled that many have secured jobs locally, in the City and as far afield as Australia, Canada and Japan. 2013 saw our first past pupil graduate from Cambridge University. We are proud that Ardleigh Green schools have laid the foundations for our children to achieve national sporting and artistic success, as well securing jobs as teachers, sports coaches, physiotherapists, journalists, television producers, dentists, carpenters, builders and decorators to name but a few. We are justifiably proud of our academic success but equally proud that we have contributed to developing polite, respectful and caring young people.
Our Vision
The vision for Ardleigh Green schools is simply:
The poem, The Guiding Hand (written by Eileen Morris) encapsulates the importance we place on establishing caring, positive and nurturing relationships with our children.
The Guiding Hand Whose hand is this that takes my own and clasps it from the hand I’ve known?Will this voice that sounds so grand, speak gently or with harsh command?Will I survive these giant places, these strange and unfamiliar faces?What is it they will expect of me? Perhaps that one and two is three.Will I cope with what is planned? Perhaps I’ll find that guiding hand.The hand that moulds and helps me see, the person I was meant to be.Will I when learning days are through say, “Teacher I remember you.” By Eileen MorrisAged 97

pageCache.pageTitle: Ardleigh Green at Home – Ardleigh Green Infant School
pageCache.text:
Ardleigh Green Infant School has developed a Home School Learning Platform to support teaching and Learning at home. The platform consists of a number of online programs which promote independent learning both at home and in school.
In addition to the Learning Platform, if your child is absent from school, specific activities are set by the class teacher either through Google Classroom or Class Dojo .
To access the platform for your child’s class:
This will take you to the Home Learning Provision for your child.
If you have any queries regarding the platform or the additional work set for your child please contact your child’s teacher via Class Do Jo.Our Home Learning Platform provides access to on-line programs. Each child is issued with a password which enables access to specific age related programs both in school and at home. The platform is designed to encourage independent learning and support programmes of study delivered by class teachers. In addition to the commercial programs used on the platform such as My Maths and Oxford Owls, the school has also produced Lyric Land and Dance Moves to support our weekly Music and Dance lessons. Subject specific platforms have been developed to enhance and extend teaching and learning both at home in school and Home Learning is also supported by the National Oak Academy which gives children access to age related learning activities across the curriculum. Our Home Learning Platform is the gateway to Remote Learning. Remote Learning takes place when a class is unable to access teaching and learning in school. Our programme of remote learning ensures the continuity of teaching and learning through the use of Google Classroom. Remote Learning was reviewed in January 2021 in line with government advice and guidance. Provision is firmly embedded throughout the school and digital devices have been made available for families who do not have access to a laptop or ipad.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years – Ardleigh Green Infant School
pageCache.text:
Aims
At Ardleigh Green Infant School, we aim to inspire and motivate pupils to develop intellectual curiosity, as they embark on their learning journey with us. We offer high quality teaching and learning, enabling pupils to develop a sense of awe and wonder, as they explore our setting. We take great pride in our spacious and well-resourced classrooms, conservatory and outstanding outdoor provision. We have a positive approach to behaviour, guiding pupils to become well-rounded, responsible members of the community, valuing themselves and others. We nurture the children as they develop relationships, learn to regulate their emotions, articulate their views using full sentences, and become confident, independent individuals.
The Learning Journey
At Ardleigh Green Infant School, children begin their learning journey in Reception. Initially we follow a carefully planned transition timetable consisting of ‘stay and play’ and independent sessions, so your child can become familiar with their new learning environment and build effective relationships with all staff across the setting.
If you are considering Ardleigh Green Infant School as the school for your child, we warmly welcome visits during our prospective parent tours, where you can have a tour around our wonderful setting, meet staff and ask questions.
How do I know if my child is ready for school?
We recognise your child’s first day at school is a huge milestone, not only for your child, but also for you as parents/carers. Please feel assured that we spend time getting to know the children during their first term and we are always happy to help if you have any questions or concerns. Every morning your child will be greeted on the door by members of our fantastic EYFS Team, to help them feel settled and ready for a busy and exciting day ahead. Sharing books together as a family and developing self-help skills such as recognising their name, dressing and undressing, feeding themselves with cutlery and toileting independently, are some of the ways you can support us in helping your child to settle quickly and feel happy and comfortable in their new setting.
The Curriculum
At Ardleigh Green we have an ambitious and exciting curriculum, enriched with opportunities for your child to develop knowledge and skills in all areas of the EYFS curriculum.

Safeguarding at Ardleigh Green Infant School
All staff at Ardleigh Green Infant School take responsibility for promoting the welfare and wellbeing of the children in our care. The Local Authority also requires that our staff safeguard the welfare of all children by referring any serious concerns that they may have to a member of the School’s Safeguarding Team. This team, who receive regular training in all matters relating to safeguarding, will always treat all information, sensitively, confidentially and in a professional manner.
Safeguarding Team

To help staff monitor the welfare of each child it is extremely important that parents keep the school informed of any unusual or serious injuries that their child has suffered and any changes that have occurred in home circumstances which might cause a child’s behaviour to change. In cases where staff have serious concerns about the welfare of a child, then the school has a duty to make a referral to Social Care. If this ever happens, please remember that it is because the school has a responsibility to promote and safeguard the welfare of every child in our care.
The school has a detailed Safeguarding Policy available on school website or from the School Office. This document outlines policies and procedures in relation to safeguarding at Ardleigh Green Infant School.
If you have any worries or concens about the welfare of a child at our school. Please contact us. All information will of course be treated in the strictest confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing for Pupils – Ardleigh Green Infant School
pageCache.text:
Caring for the health and safety of every pupil is our top priority. We want the young people in our care to be happy so that they will thrive and achieve. In the school community, some children will face difficulties at school or at home. We have support available to help with every type of problem.
ELSA
What is ELSA?
ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant) is an initiative developed and supported by educational psychologists. It recognises that children learn better and are happier in school if their emotional needs are also met. At Ardleigh Green we have a qualified Emotional Literacy Support Assistant: Mrs Peermamode. She plans and delivers programmes of support to pupils experiencing temporary or longer term emotional needs such as social skills, bereavement, anger management, self-esteem and counselling skills such as solution focus and friendship.
This leaflet for parents / carers explains some of the ways that ELSA assistants can help:
If you think that your child might benefit from this kind of help, please contact the school office.
If you or someone you know needs urgent help, please see one of our safeguarding team immediately: Mrs Hoffman or Mrs Broadmore.
